why_this_file_exists: An R-35 verifier named behaviour no commit body mentions: 69e7323 made ReceiptLedger build and drive an OutcomeLedger for every receipt walk -- that is, for every /api/calculate, /api/bis and /api/optimize request -- and OutcomeLedger's write-once discipline raises. The bodies of that slice describe the ledger as 'refusing a second answer to one question', which is the design and is right. What none of them states is the operational consequence: a condition that previously resolved silently, because the event dict simply took the last write, is now an unhandled exception on a user request. The campaign's own thesis is that a failure must be named rather than anonymous, and 'we joined a raising record to all three serving paths' is a sentence somebody owed a reader. It is written here, dated, with the raise set enumerated from source and a gate that asserts the consequence rather than describing it.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves to retired[] only when the raise set is bounded on the serving path -- either because the campaign rules these raises into the D-25 boundary shape (a named 500 carrying a receipt, the way ProjectionStarvation is handled) or because every reachable raise is proven impossible over an enumerated roster population rather than over the committed corpus alone. Deleting the entry is not closing it, and neither is widening a catch: an absorbed OutcomeRewritten is the last-write-wins the join replaced.

defects.raised_by: an R-35 verifier on slice group campaign-close, under 'behaviour the commit bodies do not mention'
defects.what: src/calculator/survival/receipt_state.py:412 constructs an OutcomeLedger inside every ReceiptLedger, so the receipt walk drives it on every request. Three of its methods raise: write() raises OutcomeRewritten on a second write to one outcome field, _claim_applied() raises DuplicateApplied on a second APPLIED claim for one (source_key, subject, event_slot), and skip() raises OutcomeRewritten on a second un-preserved skip. Before 69e7323 all three were fixture-only.
defects.why_it_matters: src/app.py wraps every registered view in exactly one catch, _within_starvation_boundary, and that catch names ProjectionStarvation alone (D-25: exactly one catch, allowlisted by a source assertion). OutcomeRewritten and DuplicateApplied are RuntimeError subclasses and are not caught anywhere on the serving path, so a request that trips one returns a bare 500 with no disposition, no receipt and no named field -- an unnamed failure, which is the shape the STARVED boundary exists to avoid.
defects.why_it_is_filed_rather_than_fixed: Both available fixes are rulings rather than lane edits. Widening the boundary to catch these is a second member of the single-catch rule D-25 states, and a lane may not extend that rule. Absorbing them instead of raising would restore the last-write-wins the join was landed to replace, which is the campaign's own failure shape. What a lane may do is measure the reachable set and say so, which is this entry.

raise_sites: src/calculator/survival/outcome_state.py:276 -- OutcomeRewritten, a second write to one outcome field
src/calculator/survival/outcome_state.py:307 -- DuplicateApplied, a second APPLIED claim for one key
measured.coverage_that_bounds_the_reachable_set: the five committed coupled scenarios, scripts/acceptance_matrix.py (10 scenarios), scripts/champion_optimizer_matrix.py (173 champions), and the E9 corpus -- all green. Nothing bounds rosters outside them.
measured.precedent_in_the_same_slice: ff5e31d found exactly this class of latent crash in the neighbouring adapter: ScoreLedger.skip had no preserve_reason parameter, 'a TypeError that had simply never been reached'. That is the argument for naming the risk rather than against it.

defects.reproducer: Construct an OutcomeLedger, write one outcome field twice on one action, and observe OutcomeRewritten; then pass that exception through src.app._within_starvation_boundary and observe that it propagates rather than becoming a receipted 500.
defects.reproducer_after_closure: Inverted: either the boundary returns a named 500 carrying the rewritten slot and field, or the raise is proven unreachable over the enumerated population rather than over the committed corpus.
defects.for_the_owner: Two questions, both above a lane. Does D-25's 'exactly one catch' rule name ProjectionStarvation specifically, or the class of programming errors a projection or a ledger raises on a request? And if the second, does the STARVED disposition cover a rewritten outcome, or does the invariant table owe a fifth spelling? Until one of those is answered the raise stands, uncaught and now recorded.
